action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up the acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both lean up, with high confidence (88/100 including today's news, 81 on market data alone), so this is a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price is only about 2% above its 50-day average and the Fed meets on 27–28 October, grow the budget in steps and keep part of it flexible to pause if price closes below $81,704 (the 50-day average). This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

reasons: Price is about 14% above its 200-day average and up 28% over 90 days.
About 71% of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average.
Price ($83,116) sits between the $81,704 50-day average and the $86,480 30-day high.

watch: The longer picture leans up, but price has gone very quiet just above its 50-day average while more people are betting on a rise than on a fall, and US Bitcoin funds saw about $487M leave in the latest day. A close below $81,704 would test the uptrend; a close above $86,480 would ease the worry.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still leans up and nothing in today's news changes that, but the past week has been a quiet pause rather than a push. Short term, the mood is warm but not reckless: the Fear & Greed reading is 63 out of 100, and price swings are about as calm as they have been all year, which often comes before a bigger move in either direction. If price closes above $86,480 (the 30-day high) the short-term picture turns clearly up; below $81,704 (the 50-day average) it turns down, and in between expect choppy days. Calm, steady campaigns fit this week; a sharp move out of that range is what would call for a change of pace.

Over the next month, the picture leans moderately up. Price is about 28% higher than three months ago and about 71% of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average, though the past week added under 2%. There is room to climb if price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high); the move fades if price slips below $81,704 (the 50-day average), only about 2% under today's $83,116. The Fed's 27–28 October meeting is the next scheduled event, and holding above the 50-day line through it would keep growth campaigns well timed.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 14% above its 200-day average, but that average is barely rising and price is still about a third below its record, so this is an early recovery rather than a mature uptrend. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,734 (the 200-day average), with $67,029 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. News is adding a little here: Switzerland's regulator approved its first fund that holds Bitcoin directly for everyday investors (PANews); a clearly rising 200-day average would strengthen this read and supports steady investment in new-user acquisition.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into growth with a steady, confident tone: the bigger trend is up, but no rally is under way and the market is unusually calm, so favour trust, access and education stories now and keep rally creatives ready in case the range breaks.
